To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) the time delay gap is a good indicator for distance in a room and 2) the direct-to-reverb ratio is a good indicator of distance in a room.
the presented algorithms change the perceived distance of auditory events in a binaural room reproduction and that the perceived distance is congruent between the listening and the synthesized room.

a) the time and energy dependent shaping of the BRIRs leads to a change of the perceived distance, b) the DRR of the BRIR can be modified to achieve congruence between listening and synthesized room and c) the congruence of the synthesized room and listening room is perceptible.
In summary, our research is concerned with
perceptual effects of distance perception and externalization by shaping binaural room-impulse responses.
perceptual distance and externalization of binaural headphone listening.
the development of a binaural synthesis of BRIRs that is capable of changing the perceived distance of an auditory source and the externalization of the auditory event in a virtual listening room.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
distance perception is influenced by a time delay gap and the direct-to-reverb ratio.
the distance perception is not only influenced by time delay gap and the direct-to-reverb-ratio, but also by other properties of the binaural room impulses.
the presented methods are useful to change the perceived direction of sound sources, the perceived distance of sound sources, and the externalization of sound sources in a binaural reproduction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presented algorithms are capable to change the distance perception and the externalization of auditory objects by changing the energy distribution of binaural impulse responses.
the presented methods are useful for a controlled modification of distance perception and externalization in binaural headphone systems.
the presented shaping algorithm allows to modify the distance perception of non-individualized BRIRs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to modify the distance perception of a room using binaural headphone technology and to synthesize binaural room acoustics with similar distance perception as the original room.
it is possible to control the distance perception by changing the time and energy based parameters of the impulse response.
a controlled change of the distance perception can be achieved with the proposed algorithm.
